Profile

I am an embedded systems engineer who likes systems that can be proven on a bench, understood in logs, and trusted on track.

Orion Racing India

Trackside embedded work with real consequences.

01

Vehicle Control Unit

Built throttle control, Ready-to-Drive sequencing, traction control, regenerative braking, thermal pump control, real-time DAQ, and wireless telemetry on NI myRIO.

02

STM32 Migration

Moved core VCU behavior to embedded C on a custom STM32H753ZI platform, with SIL and HIL validation using NUCLEO boards and STM32CubeIDE.

03

BMS and Data

Supported BMS fault detection, CAN communication, real-time monitoring, state-of-charge estimation, passive balancing, and accumulator behavior analysis.

04

Powertrain Tuning

Tuned BAMOCAR D3 parameters including PI loops, throttle transfer functions, ramp behavior, and field weakening to sharpen acceleration performance.

Embedded & vehicle software

NI myRIO, STM32, and the CAN backbone.

The Main VCU ran on an NI myRIO-1900 in LabVIEW, handling RTD sequencing, APPS plausibility, pump and brake-light control - later ported to embedded C on a custom STM32H753ZI board, bench-tested on NUCLEO hardware, with CAN data routed to a Vector logger and a custom DAQ GUI.

Motor control & powertrain

Tuning the last 26% out of acceleration.

Led tuning of the BAMOCAR D3 motor controller through NDrive - current and speed PI loops, ramp behavior, throttle transfer functions, and field weakening - cutting acceleration time from 7.2s at Formula Bharat to 5.3s at Formula Student Germany.

Selected projects

Outside the car, the same instincts show up.

Final year project

Intelligent Performer-Tracking Stage Light

Autonomous follow-spot system using UWB indoor positioning, YOLO vision, Kalman fusion, ESP32 control, DMX512 mapping, and RS-485 actuation for real-time pan/tilt tracking.

Personal build

Three-Axis Handheld Video Stabilization Gimbal

Arduino Nano, MPU6050 DMP, three servos, and a custom 3D-printed frame with PI-D control, anti-windup, and PWM slew limiting for stable handheld footage.

Processor design

Pipelined RISC-V RV32IM Processor

Five-stage RV32I/M pipeline with forwarding, stalls, branch handling, simulation verification, and FPGA validation in Xilinx Vivado.
